info.title: Homelab hub status
info.description: The homelab hub's status snapshot (status.json), written every 5 minutes on the Mac mini by the same module the hub page and the morning briefing use (hub-status.js). Read-only. Use it for: is prod healthy, are the boxes up, alerts firing, what needs the operator, OpenRouter credit and spend, disk and memory, new errors in the last 24 hours. Also the last 48 hours of events, one kind at a time (timeline/<kind>.json) for incident write-ups and 'what happened' questions. And the websites' analytics (analytics.json, Umami). And what the triage fleet wants from the operator (fleet.json).

get.summary: Current homelab status: sites, hosts, Close Listening prod health, alerts, needs-you, delivery, OpenRouter credit and spend, capacity, new errors (GlitchTip, last 24 h)
get.description: One snapshot, at most ~5 minutes old (takenAt). State values: up (green), mid (amber), down (red), stale (no recent data). Each area may be {error: ...} when its source failed; say so instead of guessing.

takenAt.description: When the snapshot was taken (UTC, ISO 8601)

sites.description: Public websites probed from outside through Cloudflare: state, up/total, down (hosts down now), avail24h (0-1), lowest, below999 (under 99.9% in 24 h), hosts[]; offline=true means the mini itself had no internet, so states are unknown

boxes.description: Collector freshness per host (mini, dgx, x3, prod): state up (<3 min), stale, down; ageSeconds

podcast.description: Close Listening prod health (daily check): state, known, stale (check not run in 26 h), ageHours, checks per area (gateway, o11y_logs, o11y_metrics, o11y_traces, o11y_glitchtip); null = no data

alerts.description: Firing alerts from Grafana: ok (false = the alert source failed), critical[], warning[] (name, instance, severity, summary, since), plumbing (wiring alerts, not incidents)

needsYou.description: What needs the operator: total, bugQueue (triage fleet's bug queue), escalations7d

delivery.description: Email/push delivery workers: state, workersUp/workers, reasons[] for amber

spend.description: OpenRouter spend: yesterdayUsd, avg7dUsd (per day), monthUsd (completed UTC days)

capacity.description: Per host (mini, dgx, prod): diskFreePct, memUsedPct (mini also swapBytes); numbers only, the alert rules decide warnings

errors.description: GlitchTip error issues first seen in the last 24 hours and still open, computed by the hub (complete, newest first): ok, windowHours, newCount, new[] (id = short id, project, title, count = occurrences, firstSeen UTC, status, link), resolvedCount (new ones already resolved or ignored: give the number, do not list them). Use this for 'what new errors appeared'; list exactly the issues in new[].

get.summary: Website analytics (Umami) per site: visitors and pageviews today, yesterday, the last 7 days and the 7 days before; the last 7 days' top pages, referrers, countries and click events; visitors on the site now
get.description: Written every 5 minutes by the hub from Umami, computed there: give the numbers as they are, never add up or estimate. The periods' exact windows are in `periods` (the operator's clock). Sites are sorted by visitors in the last 7 days. A site with `error` could not be read: say so. Countries are ISO codes (DE = Germany). Referrers leave out direct visits.

ok.description: false = Umami could not be read (reason)

periods.description: today, yesterday, last7d, previous7d: each window on the operator's clock

activeNow.description: Visitors on the site in the last 5 minutes

events.description: Click and custom events by name, e.g. cta-book-call

get.summary: What happened in the last 48 hours, one kind at a time: last-night (every kind, 19:00 to 07:00), alert, deploy, backup, drill, drift, ci_failure, error (new GlitchTip issues), container_start
get.description: Written every 5 minutes by the hub from the sources themselves. Call it with the kind the question is about: kind=alert for alerts (fired, resolved), kind=deploy for deploys, kind=last-night for anything about last night. `lines` are finished timeline lines, oldest first: '<time on the operator's clock> — <what happened> — <where to find it>'. Answer with the lines that match the question, each copied character for character, one per line: never change a time, never write a time or an event that is not in a line. An alert that fired and later resolved is over. `missing` names sources that could not be read: say so instead of claiming nothing happened.

window.description: last-night only: the window on the operator's clock

to.description: Window end (UTC), at most ~5 minutes ago

timezone.description: The time zone of the times in the lines

get.summary: What the triage fleet wants from the operator: the count (needsYou), its escalations of the last 7 days with their issues, bug proposals waiting, and every escalated issue still open
get.description: Written every 5 minutes by the hub from the fleet's own ledgers and GitHub. needsYou is the fleet's count (escalations of the last 7 days + bug proposals); give it as the number. escalations7d lists them, each with its issue (an issue can already be closed: say so). openEscalated is every escalated issue still open, of any age, newest first: the backlog. Name issues by repo and number with their url, exactly as given; never invent an issue. `unreadable` names repos GitHub refused: say their issues are missing.

needsYou.description: The fleet's count: escalations of the last 7 days + bug proposals

local.description: When the fleet escalated, on the operator's clock

issue.description: The GitHub issue: repo, number, url, state (open/closed), title; null when the fleet never filed one

bugQueue.description: Bug proposals waiting for the operator's yes: title, fingerprint, queued

repos.description: The repos the fleet files into
